business.title: The HBR Interview with Verizon CEO Dan Schulman
business.description: Following a successful nine-year stint as the CEO of PayPal, Dan Schulman was ready to retire. But after the board of Verizon repeatedly urged him to step in, he became the CEO of the telecommunications giant. His task: to turn around a company that has seen steep declines in market share, share price, and customer satisfaction. In this wide-ranging conversation with HBR’s editor at large, Schulman discusses how he’s trying to shake up Verizon’s culture. “The company had a lot to be proud of, but it was resistant to change….When the pace of change external to a company is faster than the change of pace internally, you’re falling behind.” He also reflects on both the risk and promise of AI and what it takes to be an exceptional leader.

science.title: Beyond conventional: controlled-release fertilizers maintain yield, quality, and soil health with reduced environmental footprint
science.description: Optimizing nitrogen (N) management in viticulture is crucial for sustainable grape production, particularly amidst escalating environmental concerns and climate change. This study investigated the efficacy of a Controlled-Release Nitrogen (CRN) fertilizer as a sustainable alternative to conventional mineral NPK fertilization in grapevine, applying CRN at a total dose reduced by 25% compared to the conventional NPK treatment. We comprehensively evaluated vine agronomical responses (N status, yield, grape quality), alongside environmental impacts on water resources, soil properties, and microbial communities over multiple years. Results consistently showed that CRN maintained superior vine N status, as indicated by higher SPAD values, suggesting more consistent N availability throughout the season and improved plant resilience. Crucially, despite the reduced application dosage, CRN achieved grape yields and must quality parameters (e.g., TSS, pH, acidity, YAN) comparable to the conventional NPK treatment. Furthermore, the volatile aroma profile of the grapes remained unaffected by the CRN application. Environmentally, CRN reduced nitrate leaching, decreasing nitrate concentration in water, and sustained the metabolic activity and functional diversity of soil microbes. These findings underscore CRN as a valid solution for sustainable viticulture, offering comparable productivity and quality with reduced environmental footprint and enhanced ecosystem resilience to climate change challenges.

science.title: Changes in gene expression of tyrosine hydroxylase, its regulating transcription factors, dopamine receptors in striatal neurons after their dopaminergic denervation
science.description: Among the priorities in neurology is the development of pathogenetic treatment for Parkinson’s disease (PD). Striatal neurons capable of expressing the tyrosine hydroxylase gene (Th) and containing this enzyme represent a potential target for such therapy. Transgenic mice with the green fluorescent protein gene under the Th promoter were used to model PD via 1‑methyl‑4‑phenyl‑1,2,3,6‑tetrahydropyridine neurotoxin. We aimed to determine whether reduced dopaminergic innervation of the striatum is accompanied by changes in the expression of Th and genes for transcription factors regulating its expression. Twelve hours after neurotoxin administration, one‑third of dopaminergic fibers were lost, especially around Th‑expressing neurons, while the number of Th‑expressing neurons increased 1.4‑fold. Along with increased Th expression, expression of gene for transcription factor Nurr1 rose 4‑fold, whereas the expression of Pou2f2 gene decreased twofold. The c‑Fos gene expression doubled, while c‑Jun (which, together with c‑Fos, forms the AP‑1 transcription factor) remained unchanged. In addition to characterizing the innervation of Th‑expressing striatal neurons, this study highlights Nurr1, AP‑1, and Pou2f2 as potential molecular targets for future research aimed at understanding Th regulation and the role of these neurons in preserving striatal dopamine levels upon deafferentation.

science.title: Phosphine-mediated azine C-H couplings with water and ammonia
science.description: The unique reactivity of transition metals has advanced C–H functionalization chemistry, enabling practitioners to directly modify drug and agrochemical compounds during Structure Activity Relationship (SAR) studies. These metals are particularly adept at transforming the C–H bonds of arenes and aromatic heterocycles, generating new reactions that form C–C and C–heteroatom bonds. However, among the many potential coupling partners, (hetero)arene C–H coupling reactions with water and ammonia are rare.1-5 Despite being two of the most abundant chemicals on Earth, their reactivity can be at odds with transition metal complexes and the elementary steps associated with C–O/C–N bond formation.6 We suspected that elements outside of the transition metal block might instead facilitate these reactions. Here, we show that simple triarylphosphines enable selective azine C–H coupling with water and ammonia. The reactions proceed via a distinct mechanism where pendant aldehyde and imine functional groups interconvert to acetal- and aminal-type forms, studied here both experimentally and computationally. This unusual example of neighboring group participation effectively delivers water and ammonia molecules into a P(V) coordination environment, promoting C–O and C–N bond formation via ligand-coupling reactions.7 A broad range of pyridines are compatible, as well as quinolines and diazines, and the chemistry functions as a late-stage tactic for hydroxylation and amination of complex pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals.
